claim: Plan §M4-7 'Chi tiết' bước 1: 'sửa short-circuit ở `tool-execution.ts:388-394`. Early return ở `:392` nằm trên `#displayInputVersion++` ở `:394`, nên một renderer tiêu thụ raw sẽ không repaint giữa stream' — phrased as a live defect being fixed.
verdict: MISFRAMED — the line numbers are right, the diagnosis is not
correction: The short-circuit is correct TODAY. `displayArgsForPrefix` allocates a fresh args object on every frame where the raw prefix grew (`const rawPrefixChanged = entry.exposeRawPartialJson && prefix !== entry.displayPrefix;` at :424, then a new literal at :428), returns `changed: true`, and `#tick` only calls `updateArgs` inside `if (display.changed)` (:614-616) — so args reference identity changes exactly when the raw prefix grew, and `#displayInputVersion++` does fire. The early return at :392 is sound. It becomes UNSOUND only as a consequence of step 2: once `rawArgs` is a side channel, the decoded args can be reference-identical while `rawArgs.json` grew, and the guard would swallow the frame. So step 1 is not a bug fix, it is the guard-rail that makes step 2 safe — which is why the ordering is load-bearing. The plan's own text ('nhưng phải tiến version khi chỉ phần tiền tố raw đổi') states the right requirement; only the framing as a pre-existing defect is wrong, and the comment at :388-391 ('Callers always allocate a new arg object on each streamed delta') becomes false at exactly the moment step 2 lands and must be rewritten, not preserved.
evidence: tool-args-reveal.ts:424 `const rawPrefixChanged = entry.exposeRawPartialJson && prefix !== entry.displayPrefix;`; :427-429 fresh literal + `changed: true`; :613-616 `const display = displayArgsForPrefix(...); if (display.changed) { entry.component.updateArgs(display.args, id); ... }`. tool-execution.ts:392 `if (args === this.#args) return;` sits above :394 `this.#displayInputVersion++;`, and :800 confirms the version feeds the repaint key.

claim: Command: `bun check && bun test packages/coding-agent/test/ -t 'acp'`. Testing: a snapshot/CSV test on a fixture tree with a shadowed extension.
verdict: WRONG on both counts.
correction: The test command is vacuous for this work item. `bun test -t <pattern>` filters by TEST NAME, not by filename — the existing acp tests are named after `describe("ACP agent")` (packages/coding-agent/test/acp-agent.test.ts:556), which is why `-t 'acp'` catches them. A new extensions-triage test will not be named 'acp', so this command runs none of the new code and goes green on a completely broken implementation. Replace it with `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/extensions-triage-cli.test.ts`. Separately, `bun check` runs `check:ts` AND `check:rs`; in the current environment the Rust half and `bun test` are both blocked by the unbuilt native addon, so `check:ts` is the honest gate until the addon is built. On the test style: AGENTS.md bans 'wording/defaults' assertions and snapshot-of-a-fixture tests, and demands the test defend a NAMED observable contract. So: do not snapshot the CSV/text. Assert the transformation — one row per extension keyed by id, states drawn from the real union, a shadowed row present, a policy-disabled row carrying a non-empty `disabledReason`. Text formatting is not a defended contract and asserting it would be a banned wording test.
evidence: `grep -n 'describe(' packages/coding-agent/test/acp-agent.test.ts` → :556 `describe("ACP agent")`, :2832, :3437 — names, not filenames. `grep -n '"check"\|"check:ts"\|"test"' package.json` → :89 test, :93 check, :94 check:ts. No `pi_natives` `.node` artifact found under the tree, matching the reported addon failure.

claim: New file `packages/coding-agent/src/cli/extensions-triage-cli.ts` + register it in the coding-agent command registry.
verdict: INCOMPLETE — under-specifies the file set by two.
correction: The registry does not load `-cli.ts` modules. `cli-commands.ts:99` shows the shape: `load: () => import("./commands/config").then(m => m.default)`. A new command needs THREE files plus one registry entry: (1) `src/cli/extensions-triage-cli.ts` — the implementation; (2) `src/commands/extensions-triage.ts` — the thin `Command` subclass that `export default`s it, matching the 49 existing wrappers; (3) an `extensionsTriageHelp` entry in `src/cli/command-help.ts` in the `{ description } satisfies CommandMetadata` form; (4) the `CommandEntry` in `src/cli-commands.ts`. Building only the file the plan names yields a module nothing routes to — and because a missing registry entry makes `runCli` fall through and forward the argv to the LLM as a prompt (the #1496 regression documented in that file's own header), the command would appear to work in a demo and misbehave in real use.
evidence: `sed -n '1,60p' packages/coding-agent/src/cli-commands.ts` and `grep -n -A4 'name: "config"'` → :98-101. `cat packages/coding-agent/src/commands/config.ts` shows the full wrapper→impl→helpHelp chain. `ls packages/coding-agent/src/commands/` → 49 modules; `sed -n '1,40p' packages/coding-agent/src/cli/command-help.ts` and `git grep -n -A6 'interface CommandMetadata' packages/utils/src/cli.ts` (:136-142) confirm the help shape.

claim: (Implicit) `shadowedBy` is one field with one meaning.
verdict: MISLEADING — the name is overloaded across three unrelated subsystems.
correction: Before touching this, know that `shadowedBy` already means two other things in this codebase and neither is the capability-shadowing the plan is about: marketplace plugin summaries use `shadowedBy?: "project"` (packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/marketplace/types.ts:196, documented at :188) rendered by builtin-marketplace.ts and plugin-settings.ts; and the internal user-config protocol uses `shadowedBy?: string` to mean 'your user config is overridden by your project config' (packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/cfg-protocol.ts:83, rendered at interactive-mode.ts:5970-5971). Only the tui extensions `Extension.shadowedBy` is the one this item is about. Conflating them is the easiest mistake in this file and would produce an inventory that reports plugin-scope shadowing as if it were capability shadowing.
evidence: `git grep -rn 'shadowedBy' -- packages/` returns 35 hits across six distinct subsystems; the three cited above are at marketplace/types.ts:196, cfg-protocol.ts:83, and tui/overlays/extensions/types.ts:68 respectively.
